findings.rule: D41/D42: confirm the named skill the user saw and answered; no regression vs 348a4947
findings.trigger: strictCanonicalsIn drops every loose-alias term, including surfaces that contain the display form verbatim. termsIn keeps the longest overlap, so 'Core Java' consumes 'Java' and then gets filtered out, which leaves Java unstated. Probes at a859ae29 return [] where 348a4947 returned the skill: stated('Java','Wrote Core Java services'), stated('Android','Did Android development for 5 years'), stated('Tally','Used Tally ERP 9 daily'), stated('Excel','Advanced Excel modelling'), stated('Supply Chain','Led supply chain management'), stated('SAP','Ran SAP FICO'), stated('.NET','Built .NET Core APIs'), stated('C','Wrote C programming labs'), stated('iOS','iOS development lead'). isNamedSkillKeyword is also false for 'java' in 'Strong Core Java skills', 'android' in 'Android development experience', 'tally' in 'Proficiency in Tally ERP 9' and 'excel' in 'Advanced Excel required'. The offline extractor emits exactly those canonicals from those surfaces, and they are common in fresher JDs, so a YES answer adds no keyword to coverage and AddUserStatedFactUseCase records nothing. No truth risk, because these are false negatives.
findings.proof: Fix: treat a loose surface as loose only when it does not contain the display as whole words. In SkillLexicon.isLooseAlias: `val entry = entriesByCanonical[term.canonical] ?: return false; val surface = keyOf(term.surface); return entry.looseAliases.any { keyOf(it) == surface } && !" $surface ".contains(" ${keyOf(entry.display)} ")`. That keeps SwiftUI, Shell scripting, AngularJS, HTML5, es6 and microservice loose. Note that 'angular js' (with a space) would then state Angular. Pin it either way, or drop that alias. Tests: stated('Java','Wrote Core Java services')==[Java], stated('Tally','Used Tally ERP 9 daily')==[Tally], isNamedSkillKeyword(req('Strong Core Java skills','java'),'java')==true, plus the existing looseAliasesDoNotResolveToAnotherSkill.
findings.title: Loose aliases that contain the skill name ('Core Java', 'Tally ERP 9', 'Android development', 'Advanced Excel') no longer state that skill

findings.rule: Constitution I.1 (a false confirm or false evidence is a truth violation)
findings.trigger: The case-sensitive bare exactForms 'Go' and 'Express' sit in the global lexicon, so they affect more than keywordsStatedIn. They also reach EvidenceIndex and OfflineGapMatcher (bound in DomainModule:41 and used by prod RemoteJobAnalysisSource), RequirementExtractor and ClauseEmphasiser. Sentence-initial and proper-noun uses match. In keywordsStatedIn, 'Go to the client site weekly', 'Go through reports', 'Go above and beyond', 'Played Pokemon Go', 'Express delivery handled', 'Worked at American Express' and 'Applied via Express Entry' confirm Go or Express. That path is low likelihood, because the statement answers the Go or Express question. The evidence path is likelier: a resume line 'Senior Analyst, American Express' yields canonical express, so a JD 'Express' (Node) requirement becomes MET with the AmEx entry as evidence, and the app never asks the candidate. 'Visual Studio Express' and 'SQL Server Express' do the same. The offline JD analyser turns 'Go above and beyond' into a Go SKILL requirement. Blocked-suffix lists cannot cover sentence-initial imperatives.
findings.proof: Fix: give the exact form a required positive context instead of more blocklists. Add `val requiredPrefix: String? = null` to LexiconEntry. In TermPattern.build, prepend `(?<=$it)` only for the exactForms pattern. Set it for Go and Express to `(?:\b(?:in|with|using|and|or)\s|[,/(:]\s?)`. Keep the existing '-', 'live', 'to market' and 'interest' blocks. Result: 'Built services in Go', 'Experience with Go', 'Python, Go and Java', 'APIs with Express' and 'Node.js/Express' match. Sentence-initial 'Go to…'/'Go through…', 'Pokemon Go', 'Let's Go!', 'American Express', 'Visual Studio Express', 'Express delivery' and 'Express Entry' do not. Line-initial skills lists such as 'Go, Python' become a false negative, which is safe. Tests in KeywordsStatedInTest: stated('Go','Go to the client site weekly')==[], stated('Go','Go through reports')==[], stated('Express','Worked at American Express')==[], stated('Express','Express delivery handled')==[]. In SkillLexiconTest: canonicalsIn('Senior Analyst, American Express')==[].
findings.title: Bare 'Go'/'Express' exact forms match sentence-initial verbs and proper nouns ('Go through reports', 'American Express') lexicon-wide
